lines: +description: Use the @nx/directive-checks lint rule on ESLint or Oxlint to report @nx- directives that Nx ignores and project patterns that match no project.
+The `@nx/directive-checks` lint rule checks the `@nx-` directives in the comment block that
+- `@nx-depends-on` and `@nx-ignore-server-inputs` scope the task of a split end-to-end (e2e)
+  test file to the code the test exercises.
+  To learn how to use them, see [skip unaffected split e2e tests](/docs/kb/skip-unaffected-e2e-tests).
+- `@nx-target-name` names the task of a script that the `@nx/js/node` or `@nx/js/tsx` plugin
+When Nx can't read a directive, it ignores it silently or with a warning that's easy to miss.
+An ignored `@nx-depends-on` or `@nx-ignore-server-inputs` leaves the test's task unscoped, so
+the test reruns on every change to the app.
+The rule isn't in the shared configs that `@nx/eslint-plugin` exports, and generators don't
+Add it to the root lint config that project configs extend.
+For ESLint, that's `eslint.base.config.mjs` when the workspace has one, and
+On Oxlint, the rule comes from the same JavaScript plugin as `@nx/enforce-module-boundaries`.
+For how Nx runs Oxlint, see [Nx with Oxlint](/docs/technologies/oxlint/introduction).
+The entry has no `files` pattern, so the rule runs on every file the config already lints,
+A `files` pattern would make ESLint lint files that match it, even ones the config sets no
+The rule reads the project graph only for files whose opening comments contain
+When you update Nx with `nx migrate`, a migration in `@nx/eslint` adds the rule to the root
+It does so when a split test file already has `@nx-depends-on` or `@nx-ignore-server-inputs`
+and no ESLint config mentions the rule yet.
+The config must also register the `@nx` plugin for every file, as the configs Nx generates do.
+When the migration can't verify that, it prints a warning instead.
+Add the rule to a config that registers `@nx` for the files it checks.
+Nx reads directives only from the comment block that opens a file, before the first line of
+Blank lines, a `#!` line, and other comments can come first.
+The rule reports a comment line shaped like a directive, `@nx-<name>` alone or followed by a
+colon, when Nx doesn't read that name.
+If the name is close to a directive Nx reads, the message suggests it:
+`"@nx-depend-on" is not a directive Nx reads, so Nx ignores it. Did you mean "@nx-depends-on"?`
+A line with more text after the name and no colon, such as `// @nx-todo check the flaky step`,
+isn't shaped like a directive, so the rule doesn't report it.
+After the first line of code, the rule reports an unknown name only when it can suggest a directive.
+A misspelled `// @nx-depend-on: checkout` after an import is reported, and `// @nx-flaky` isn't.
+The rule reports a known directive that Nx can't parse, such as `@nx-depends-on` without its
+The message names the form Nx reads, such as `Write it as "@nx-depends-on: <project>, <project>".`
+The rule also reports a directive in a comment after code, such as after an import or a
+It also reports a directive on the line where a block comment ends and code follows the `*/`.
+Move the directive above the first line of code:
+The rule reports a directive whose value Nx ignores:
+| Reported line                                                       | Why Nx ignores it                          | Fix                                                         |
+| `// @nx-depends-on:`                                                | It lists no projects.                      | List the projects the test depends on, separated by commas. |
+| `// @nx-ignore-server-inputs: true`                                 | The directive takes no value.              | Write `// @nx-ignore-server-inputs` alone.                  |
+| `// @nx-target-name:`                                               | The task name is empty.                    | Write the task name after the colon.                        |
+| A second `// @nx-target-name: start` after `@nx-target-name: serve` | Nx reads only the first `@nx-target-name`. | Remove the extra line.                                      |
+Nx merges every `@nx-depends-on` line, so the rule reports empty `@nx-depends-on` lines only when
+none of the lines in the file lists a project.
+These checks run on a test file that a split task runs.
+The checks read the cached project graph.
+A plugin can record on each split task the test file it runs and the directives it applies.
+The Playwright, Cypress e2e, and Jest plugins record them with `applyTestFileDirectives` from
+`@nx/devkit/internal`, which other plugins can also call.
+When no split task records the file, the rule looks for a split task that records no file and
+Vitest and Cypress component test split tasks record nothing, so the rule finds them this way.
+A name can also end with another file's path, so the rule can
+[check a file that no split task runs](#limits).
+Nx applies both directives to Playwright and Cypress e2e split tasks, and only `@nx-depends-on`
+It applies neither to Vitest or Cypress component test split tasks.
+The rule reports a directive that the file's split task doesn't record as applied.
+For a Jest test file, list the projects the test exercises instead:
+`No split task that runs this file applies "@nx-ignore-server-inputs", so Nx ignores it.`
+For a Vitest or Cypress component test file, remove the directive.
+When several split tasks run the same file, the rule reports a directive only if none of them
+It then doesn't report the directive's value, since Nx ignores the whole directive.
+### Project patterns that match no project
+The rule matches each `@nx-depends-on` pattern against the project graph the way Nx does when
+A pattern can be an exact project name, a name with a `name:`, `tag:`, or `directory:` prefix,
+A pattern that matches no project makes every Nx command that includes the task fail, unless it's
+A target default or `project.json` entry that replaces the task's `inputs` without `"..."` drops
+Nx then doesn't check the patterns, so an unmatched pattern fails no command.
+The rule still reports it, because the pattern fails commands once the entry keeps `"..."`.
+When a project name is close, the message suggests it, such as the full name `@acme/shop-ui`
+`"shop-ui" matches no project. Did you mean "@acme/shop-ui"?`

+- The rule reads the project graph that Nx cached last.
+  A pattern that names a project created after that reads as matching no project until Nx
+- When the rule matches split tasks to the file and none of them records a directive as applied,
+  it reports the directive as ignored, even when a plugin applies it.
+- For a split task that records no test file, the rule goes by the task name, which can end with
+  For example, the Vitest task `test-ci--checkout--unit.spec.ts` runs `checkout--unit.spec.ts`,
+  but its name also ends with `unit.spec.ts`.
+  The rule then reports a test directive in `unit.spec.ts` as ignored.
+  Nx does ignore it there, since no split task runs that file.
+- A lint task's hash covers the e2e project and the projects it depends on.
+  The rule also reads other projects, such as an API that `@nx-depends-on` names but the e2e
+  After a rename of that project, `nx lint` can replay a cached clean result.
+  `nx affected -t lint` doesn't run the e2e project's lint task at all.
+  To check again, run the lint task with `--skip-nx-cache`.
+  The e2e task still fails before it runs, with an error that names the pattern.

The directives require Nx 24 or later. Check the workspace's `nx` version first. On an older version, stop and report that the workspace needs to upgrade.

-1. Find the e2e projects and their split targets with `nx show project <e2e-project> --json`. Split targets are named `e2e-ci--<test file path>`. If there are none, stop. Cypress creates them only when the `nxE2EPreset` options set `ciWebServerCommand`, and Vitest and Cypress component tests don't read the directives.

+1. Find the e2e projects and their split targets with `nx show project <e2e-project> --json`. Split targets are named `<ciTargetName>--<test file path>`, where `ciTargetName` is the Playwright or Cypress plugin option in `nx.json` and defaults to `e2e-ci`. If there are none, stop. Cypress creates them only when the `nxE2EPreset` options set `ciWebServerCommand`, and Vitest and Cypress component tests don't read the directives.
2. Before editing any files, ask the user to choose a scoping approach and wait for their answer:
- **A. Project-based scoping with `@nx-depends-on` (recommended).** Explicitly list the projects each test exercises. The projects they depend on are included automatically.

- **B. Import-based scoping with `@nx-ignore-server-inputs` (advanced).** Use only when we understand exactly what each test depends on, Ultracache is enabled in Nx Cloud, the runner is Playwright or Cypress, and the imports capture everything needed to invalidate its cached result.

+7. On Nx 24.1 or later, enable the `@nx/directive-checks` lint rule in the root lint config unless it's already enabled, then run the e2e projects' lint tasks and fix every problem the rule reports. On Nx 24.0, skip this step, because the rule ships in Nx 24.1. To enable the rule:

+   - ESLint: in the root config that project configs extend, add an entry `{ rules: { '@nx/directive-checks': 'error' } }` with no `files` pattern. That config is `eslint.base.config.mjs` when it exists, else `eslint.config.mjs`. With `.eslintrc.json` configs, add the rule to the top-level `rules` of `.eslintrc.base.json` when it exists, else `.eslintrc.json`.
+   - Oxlint: in the root `.oxlintrc.json`, add `"@nx/oxlint/boundaries-plugin"` to `jsPlugins` and `"@nx/directive-checks": "error"` to `rules`.

+8. Verify with `nx show target inputs <e2e-project>:<split target> --check <file the test exercises> <file it doesn't>`. With `@nx-depends-on`, the first file is an input and the second isn't. For `@nx-ignore-server-inputs`, run the target in CI, then inspect its Ultracache configuration in the Nx Cloud UI. Check that it includes the files the test exercises and excludes unrelated files. If the configuration isn't scoped as expected:

- Playwright: Nx runs the `webServer` as a task only when `reuseExistingServer` is `true`, the entry sets no `wait` or `env`, and `command` is `nx run <project>:<target>` or `nx <target> <project>` with no other arguments. Nx evaluates the config with its own environment, so `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI` is `false` in CI. Without a server task, `@nx-ignore-server-inputs` has no effect.

- An `nx.json` target default that matches the split target, such as one keyed `e2e-ci--*`, replaces the inferred `inputs` and `dependsOn`. Add `"..."` to each array it sets, and set `"inputs": false` on any server dependency it adds.

- If the test needs server environment variables, runtime inputs or external dependencies that the imports do not capture, report the limitation and recommend `@nx-depends-on` only if it covers those dependencies; otherwise leave the test unscoped.

-8. Do not create shared dependency groups, named inputs, target defaults, or blanket dependency lists to compensate for missing coverage. For example, do not introduce a `shopE2eRuntime` input. Report the limitation instead of inventing shared configuration.

-9. Prefer directives over `project.json` entries. A `project.json` entry under the split target's name replaces the inferred `inputs` and `dependsOn`, so copy every entry you keep and don't add `"..."`. The entry stops matching when the test file moves.
